verdicts.reason: Both are nearly the same layout. The 'See the List' CTA sits above the headline, in the wrong reading order and pushed to the left off the centred axis. Headline, body copy and footer are jammed into the top third, and the 'recommending.' orphan breaks the body copy. The small book floats in the bottom half with empty space beside it.

A keeps the book → headline → copy order and spreads the elements down the canvas. But its CTA is still stranded at the top-left above the book, off the centred axis. B crams the CTA, headline and copy against the top edge, leaves dead space around the small book, and has the same 'recommending.' orphan.

A is just the tall original shrunk to fit. The body copy and the 'Inkwell & Lantern' footer drop to roughly 6px and are hard to read, and wide empty sides remain: no real rearrangement. B rebuilds it as a proper side-by-side banner with a large book and readable text. Its flaws are a CTA moved up to the top-right corner above the headline (wrong order, detached from the copy) and a tightly packed text column.

A is a shrunk copy of the tall layout. The body and footer text are tiny, likely too small to read, and the narrow centred column wastes the sides. B's text is readable, but the CTA comes before the headline, everything is crammed at the top, and the small book floats over dead space below.
